reason: Rank the general-size fused transpose-and-pack idea first because it targets the separate A transpose and subsequent packed-A use across supported sizes. Its key risk is that the kernel may still need the same data movement, so the benefit is unknown. Next, test the TB descriptor with a timed A transpose: it may skip generated B packing, but its conversion and added A packing may outweigh that. The assembly_audit proposal is the same TB experiment, so keep it adjacent as a duplicate rather than independent evidence. The remaining A-related proposals add larger conversion costs or have less defined mechanisms. The 320-byte scratch layout is distinct from the rejected 272-byte layout, but raises scratch beyond the supplied P-core L1D size and has unknown cache mapping. The other proposals focus on B packing or output-store order. Supplied measurements show noisy overlaps and no promotion for prior candidates; none establishes causality or speedup.
